scope: Pilot: Abuja, AMAC and Bwari Area Councils
method: Each source was requested once on the retrieval date. A passage counts as verified only if it appears, word for word, in the visible text of the retrieved page (tags removed, whitespace collapsed). raw_page_sha256 hashes the exact bytes received and will differ if the site changes its markup; the passage hash is the stable evidence. Sources that blocked the request were not bypassed.

projects.title: Saburi I and II Access Road
projects.status_basis: A source reports the minister saying the road was completed and inaugurated; one media source only, so a reviewer must confirm.

facts.statement: Punch reports that the FCT minister described a 5km access road to Saburi I and II in Abuja Municipal Area Council as one of a list of roads completed and inaugurated.

passages.text: I want to inform you that these roads have all been completed and inaugurated.
Others are the 5km access road to Saburi I and II in Abuja Municipal Area Council and another 5-kilometre road in Abaji Area Council.

facts.note: One independent media source, reporting the minister's statement.

unresolved_gaps: The road's budget or contract value is not stated in the source.
The user-supplied phrase 'emergency satellite town interventions' does not appear in the fetched passages and is not used.

fictional_reports.label: FICTIONAL REPORT FIXTURE
fictional_reports.text: A community submission claims that heavy rains have washed away a section of the road shoulder near Saburi II.
fictional_reports.maintainer_review: The wording refers to a real place or facility; decide whether to make it generic before any use.

projects.title: Bwari Township Water Supply Network
projects.status_basis: The source says the network was commissioned. Commissioning is not recorded as completion, so no completion is claimed.

facts.statement: Abuja Times reports that the President commissioned the 198-kilometre Bwari Township Water Supply Network Project in the FCT (article dated 15 July 2026).

passages.text: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has commissioned the 198-kilometre Bwari Township Water Supply Network Project in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT)

facts.statement: Abuja Times quotes the President as saying the network, constructed by China Geo-engineering Construction (CGC) Nigeria Limited, connects Bwari Township and surrounding communities to the Lower Usuma Dam.

passages.text: Tinubu explained that the newly commissioned water supply network, constructed by China Geo-engineering Construction (CGC) Nigeria Limited, connects Bwari Township and surrounding communities directly to the Lower Usuma Dam, the FCT’s primary source of treated water.

unresolved_gaps: The contract cost is not stated in the passages used.
The submitted draft's phrase 'to improve access to clean water' is not in the source; the article says the President described it as a step towards improving residents' quality of life.

projects.title: Gaba-Tokulo Road
projects.status_basis: Two publishers report the road as completed and commissioned; both report the minister's statements.

facts.statement: Punch reports the minister listing a 7.2 km Gaba and Tokulo Road in Bwari Area Council among roads completed and inaugurated.

passages.text: I want to inform you that these roads have all been completed and inaugurated.
He identified the roads as the 9km Paikon Kore to Ibwa Road in Gwagwalada Area Council, and 7.2 km Gaba and Tokulo Road in Bwari Area Council.

facts.note: One media source for the length. The 7.2 km figure is in this article, not in The Nation's.

facts.statement: The Nation quotes the minister as saying the Gaba-Tokulo road project alone cost the government no less than N7 billion.

passages.text: “This Gaba-Tokulo road project alone cost the government no less than N7 billion. Since we flagged it off in January 2024, we ensured prompt payments, which allowed for timely completion without delays or abandoned contracts,” Wike stated.

facts.note: A quoted figure of cost to the government; it is not a contract value.

facts.statement: The Nation and Punch each report that the Gaba-Tokulo road in Bwari was commissioned or completed and inaugurated.

passages.text: Speaking during the commissioning of the Gaba-Tokulo road project in Bwari, Wike emphasised the administration’s commitment to delivering tangible development to every area council.
I want to inform you that these roads have all been completed and inaugurated.
He identified the roads as the 9km Paikon Kore to Ibwa Road in Gwagwalada Area Council, and 7.2 km Gaba and Tokulo Road in Bwari Area Council.

facts.note: Two publishers, but both report the same minister; whether they are materially independent needs reviewer judgement.

facts.statement: The Nation reports that the contractor was directed to provide streetlights on the road beyond the initial contract scope.

passages.text: He also commended Setraco, the construction company, for delivering a high-quality road project, adding that the contractor has been directed to also provide streetlights on the road, beyond the initial scope of the contract.

facts.note: A directive, not a report that streetlights exist.

unresolved_gaps: No date is given for the streetlights.
The article also mentions a plan to extend the road to Kawu; no timeline is stated.
The submitted draft's 'contract cost of N7 billion' is worded here as the quoted cost to the government.

fictional_reports.label: FICTIONAL REPORT FIXTURE
fictional_reports.text: A reviewer notes a submission claiming the promised streetlights along the road have not been installed.
fictional_reports.maintainer_review: The wording refers to a real place or facility; decide whether to make it generic before any use.
